clips.title: Write the Docs Portland 2017: Treating Documentation like Code: a Practical Account by Jodie Putrino
clips.why: The brain is "docs like code": pages in git, changed by pull request, checked in CI. Jodie Putrino explains what that means and why teams do it.
look: What treating documentation like code means in practice: the same tools, reviews and pipelines as the code.
The reasons she gives for the change. Which of them matter even more when the reader is an agent?
clips.after: rnd-kb is a repo like any other: a page changes through a pull request, kb lint runs as a required check, and one person approves.

clips.title: Pydantic Tutorial • Solving Python's Biggest Problem
clips.why: A clear first look at Pydantic: declare a model with types, validate data against it, and read the errors. If you know zod, this is the same idea in Python.
look: How a model is declared as a class with typed fields, like z.object() with its keys.
What happens when the data is wrong: Pydantic raises an error that names each bad field.
How fields get extra rules beyond the type, like our pattern for sources.
clips.after: Our Page model is exactly this: every brain tool calls Page.model_validate on a page's frontmatter, and lint prints each error as path:line: message.

clips.title: Finally, an Open Standard for the Karpathy LLM Wiki is HERE
clips.why: Outside our company, people who build markdown knowledge bases for agents reached the same idea: plain markdown pages with YAML frontmatter that records where facts came from and when they go stale.
look: Which fields a standard for agent-read pages puts in the frontmatter, and which of them match our owner, reviewed, confidence and sources.
Why provenance (where a fact came from) and freshness are part of the format, not an afterthought.
clips.after: Our Page model is a stricter version of the same idea: an owner who answers for the page, a review date that fades into low confidence, and at least one source.

practice.q: Nova finds two pages about CI. Which one should it trust more?

options.text: A long, detailed wiki page with no owner, no review date and no sources
options.why: Detail is not trust. Nobody answers for it, and nothing says whether it is still true.

options.text: A short brain page owned by @RhinoHealth/devops, reviewed this month at confidence high, with a link to the workflow files
options.why: It says who stands behind it, when they checked, and where to check the facts yourself.

options.text: Whichever page ranks first in search
options.why: Ranking says a page matches the words of the question, not that it is true. The trust label is a separate signal.

practice.q: Finish the line in the Page model that turns a misspelled key into a validation error.
practice.hint: Pydantic has three choices: ignore, allow and one more.
practice.why: forbid rejects any key the model does not declare, so confidense fails instead of being dropped silently.

practice.q: A page was reviewed on 1 January with review_every: 90d. After how many days without a review does effective_confidence() start returning low?
practice.hint: The rule is "more than twice overdue".
practice.why: 2 × 90 = 180. Before that the page is only overdue, which is a warning and a reminder to the owner.

practice.q: An engineer knows a fact from experience and writes a page with sources: []. Lint fails. What is the right fix?

options.text: Add sources: [me], because the author is the source
options.why: That fails the source pattern, and it gives a reader nothing to check.

options.text: Link where the fact can be checked: the code, a PR, a Jira ticket or a public thread
options.why: A source is for the reader. If nothing can be linked, the fact is a good thing to write into a ticket or a decision record first.

options.text: Set confidence: low, which allows an empty source list
options.why: The model requires at least one source at every confidence level.

practice.q: Put the life of a new brain page in order, from writing it to agents reading it.
items: The author copies templates/page.md and fills in the frontmatter and the body
The author opens a pull request in rnd-kb
kb lint validates every page against the Page model and checks owners, dates, links and paths
The required check is green and one other person approves
The page is merged, and search, Nova and the bot can read it
practice.why: Nothing reaches a reader without passing the lint and a person's review, which is what makes the trust label worth reading.
